arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Staver argued the display contains a universally recognized symbol of law.
Mr. Staver noted the Ten Commandments occupy only one-tenth of the display.
Mr. Friedman stated the County posted the display three times in a year.
Mr. Clement compared the display to the creche in Lynch v. Donnelly.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: McCreary County posted a Ten Commandments display in its courthouse. The ACLU sued to remove it. The Sixth Circuit agreed with the ACLU. The County now asks the Supreme Court to reverse that lower-court action.
